title: Built a free SEC EDGAR insider-trading pipeline (Form 4 + 8-K + 13F + 13D/G + FINRA short vol) — architecture, parsing gotchas, and what it actually surfaces
author: Cold-Fix-884
selftext:
Wanted an insider-flow signal without paying for Kestrel/Quiver/WhaleWisdom.

All the data is free at [data.sec.gov](http://data.sec.gov) but the parsing is annoying enough that

most retail tools don't bother. Wrote a Python pipeline that ingests + scores

Form 4 filings, 8-Ks (filtered by item code), 13F holdings, 13D/G stakes,

and FINRA daily short volume. Runs on my box, no external DB, \~1500 LOC.



Sharing the architecture + the landmines because I would've saved 2 days

if someone had written this post before I started.



\*\*Architecture (all Python stdlib + one requests call):\*\*



insider\_feed.py     Form 4 fetcher + role-weighted cluster detector

sec\_filings.py      8-K / 13F / 13D-G — shares insider\_feed's HTTP layer

congress\_feed.py    House PTR bulk zip parser (STOCK Act)

short\_interest.py   FINRA daily CNMSshvol pipe-delimited files

signal\_tracker.py   logs every emitted signal + backfills price outcome



Scheduled tasks (Windows Task Scheduler) fire each feed at its natural

cadence. No queue, no broker, no docker. State lives in CSVs on disk.



\*\*Landmines that cost me time:\*\*



1. \*\*The old EDGAR atom feed returns 0 entries for Form 4 as of 2024.\*\*

   Everyone's tutorials still reference cgi-bin/browse-edgar?action=getcompany

   — that endpoint's Form 4 filter is broken. Switch to:

   \`https://data.sec.gov/submissions/CIK{cik\_padded\_to\_10}.json\`

   Returns all recent filings as parallel arrays (form\[\], accessionNumber\[\],

   filingDate\[\], primaryDocument\[\]).



2. \*\*Form 4 primaryDocument is often the xsl-styled path (\`xslF345X06/foo.xml\`)

   not the raw XML.\*\* The raw XML is at the same accession URL WITHOUT the

   \`xslF345X06/\` prefix. If you fetch primaryDocument directly you get an

   XSL-transformed HTML view that ElementTree chokes on. Strip the prefix:



   \`\`\`python

   raw\_doc = pdoc.split("/", 1)\[1\] if pdoc.startswith("xsl") else pdoc



3. SEC requires a User-Agent header with a contact email. Bare requests

get 403'd. Also enforce \~4.5 req/sec (10 is the documented ceiling but

they will bounce you if you burst).

4. FINRA killed the bi-monthly short-INTEREST file (shrt{ymd}.txt is

403 now, moved behind OAuth). But the daily short-VOLUME files are still

public at cdn.finra.org/equity/regsho/daily/CNMSshvol{ymd}.txt. Different

metric (fraction of daily volume sold short, not total short interest)

but usable as a pressure proxy.

5. FINRA daily files emit floats, not ints. int(parts\[2\]) throws

ValueError on rows like "343899.973577". Cast float first. This bug

silently dropped 90% of my rows on first run.

6. 13F value column semantics changed in 2022 — pre-2022 filings report

in $1000s, post-2022 in raw $. My heuristic: treat < $10M as thousands,

▎ = $10M as raw. Not perfect but survives edge cases.

7. Windows Task Scheduler's cp1252 stdout will crash on any unicode in

your prints. Add this to every top-level script:



sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")

sys.stderr.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace")



Cluster detection scoring:



Naive "N insiders bought in last 30d" is too flat. My version weights each

insider by role:

CEO / Chief Executive:      2.5

CFO / Chief Financial:      2.2

President / Chairman:       2.0

COO / Chief Operating:      1.8

Officer:                    1.5

Director:                   1.0

cluster\_role\_score = sum(role\_weights). A CEO+CFO cluster (4.7) is a

much stronger signal than 3 directors (3.0), even though naive count would

say the opposite.



Window is 60 days, not the classic 30. Insider filings dribble in over

weeks — 30d misses real campaigns.

Signals it actually surfaces (real, current data):

\- 1 active cluster: BSX (3 directors, $554K in mid-May)

\- 0 CEO/CFO open-market buys past 30d

\- \~300 priority 8-K filings ingested last 5d

\- Top short pressure right now: DE (65.2%), IBM (62.6%), CAT (62.6%),

AMGN (62.2%)

\- 0 active "squeeze combos" (cluster + short vol >= 50%)

What I would do differently:

\- Skip 13F entirely. Delta-vs-prior-quarter is noisy, filings lag 45d,

and famous filers (Berkshire, Renaissance, Scion) mostly hold. Not the

edge people think it is.

\- Would've reached for asyncio + httpx from day 1 instead of urllib.request.

Cluster scan across 100 tickers is IO-bound and takes \~2 min sync;

could be 15-20s async.

\- Store transactions in SQLite not CSV. CSV dedupe on write is O(n) per

row and gets slow past \~50K rows.

Happy to share more specifics if useful — parsing edge cases, rate limiting

strategy, or the classification logic.

replies.author: Cold-Fix-884
replies.body:
Every ticker that gets flagged in a brief (cluster buy, exec buy,

squeeze combo, whatever) gets logged to a CSV with the price at

time-of-call. Then a scheduled job fetches current prices, computes

% return, and marks each signal as HIT / MISS / PENDING based on

whether the stock moved in the direction called by at least 3%.



It also builds a public HTML page showing every signal ever called —

hits and misses both, no cherry-picking. If a signal missed, it stays

in the log. That's how anyone can actually verify the framework

without taking my word for it.



No public repo yet — code's opinionated for my \~100-ticker universe

and needs cleanup. But DM your email and I'll send you the standalone

Form 4 + signal\_tracker files. Both are short (\~200 LOC each) and

run without the rest of my infra.
